title: Error classification convention: DownstreamError vs plain error
answers: How should I return an error from a datasource query handler?
Why do some tsdb errors use ErrorResponseWithErrorSource?
body: Failures caused by the remote/downstream system (network errors, upstream 5xx, malformed response) should be wrapped with backend.DownstreamError(err); bugs in Grafana's own code use plain errors or backend.PluginError(err). Per-query errors are returned via backend.ErrorResponseWithErrorSource(backend.DownstreamError(err)) — see pkg/tsdb/graphite/query.go:91,265,277. This classification feeds Grafana's error-source attribution/alerting UI, so returning a bare error where a downstream failure occurred loses that signal. This pattern is used broadly (83 hits across pkg/tsdb, including cloudwatch and azuremonitor).
applies: Applies to errors returned from a tsdb Service's query/resource/health handlers that are surfaced to the query response; internal bugs in Grafana's own code should not use DownstreamError.
